_meta.title: San Diego local e-bike layer (North County focus)
_meta.checked_by: Verifier pass on Oct 16, 2026, then an independent skeptic pass on Oct 19, 2026 that reread every San Diego record against enacted ordinance, code, board and statute text.

verified_values.statute_verified: The rule was read in enacted statute or ordinance text.
verified_values.secondary_only: Read only on an official city, county or district page, a press release or news. The enacted ordinance or board policy text was not read.
verified_values.unclear: Could not confirm whether a local rule exists.

_meta.how_to_use: Apply the statewide_baseline rules everywhere in California, then the record for the place the family rides. A local record never relaxes a state rule. The under-12 power in VC 21214.7 is repealed Jan 1, 2029.
notes_on_inputs: ideas_red_team.md says VC 312.5(a) requires a motor 'under 750 watts'. The current text (SB 1271, effective Jan 1, 2025) says 'does not exceed 750 watts', so exactly 750 W qualifies. 'Less than 750 watts' was the pre-2025 wording, which the Carlsbad and Encinitas pages still repeat.

ideas_red_team.md gives a second reading of Jun 30, 2026 for the City of San Diego (from NBC 7). The City's own Jun 23 release says Jul 7, 2026. The City's Aug 7 release gives the effective date as Aug 13, 2026.
ideas_red_team.md left Carlsbad's effective date open. Carlsbad's Feb 25, 2026 news post says Mar 26, 2026, with warnings until May 25, 2026.

ideas_red_team.md left open whether state law bars Class 3 from Class I bike paths. It does not since AB 1909 (effective Jan 1, 2023). VC 21207.5(b) lets locals ban e-bikes or a class on equestrian, hiking and recreational trails, and VC 21206 lets locals regulate operation on bicycle facilities.
ideas_red_team.md said AB 2595 was signed in early October 2026. leginfo shows it approved Sep 30, 2026 (Stats. 2026, ch. 843).

verification_levels.primary_verified: Every rule that can change a verdict was read in enacted ordinance, code, resolution, board or statute text, and the record lists those sources. A few notes also cite an official page, and their source_type says so.
verification_levels.primary_partial: Some rules were read in enacted text. Others rest only on an official web page.
verification_levels.primary_not_found: The enacted text behind the record was not found.

statewide_baseline.quote: A local authority within the County of San Diego, or the County of San Diego in unincorporated areas, may, by ordinance or resolution, prohibit a person under 12 years of age from operating a class 1 or 2 electric bicycle.
statewide_baseline.notes: First 60 days warnings only, then a $25 infraction. No court record if a parent shows a completed e-bike safety program within 120 days. Parent jointly liable. Current text amended by AB 1170 (Stats. 2025, ch. 67), effective Jan 1, 2026.

statewide_baseline.quote: A person under 18 years of age shall not operate a bicycle ... upon a street, bikeway ... or any other public bicycle path or trail unless they are wearing a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet
A person under 16 years of age shall not operate a class 3 electric bicycle.
statewide_baseline.notes: 21213(b) also requires a helmet for every Class 3 operator and passenger.

statewide_baseline.quote: operating a vehicle with fewer than four wheels that does not meet the definition of an electric bicycle ... capable of exclusively propelling the vehicle in excess of 20 miles per hour ... not licensed to operate the vehicle
statewide_baseline.notes: Added by AB 875 (Stats. 2025, ch. 168). Also allows removal of a Class 3 ridden by someone under 16. From Jan 1, 2027, SB 1167 (Stats. 2026, ch. 846, approved Sep 30, 2026) amends two sections. SEC. 42 amends VC 23135, which already exists for modified mopeds, adding a bar on any 2- or 3-wheeled electric device able to exceed 20 mph on motor power alone on highways unless it fits a road-legal class. SEC. 41 amends this section, adding 22651.08(a)(3), removal of an unauthorized device on a highway or public right-of-way.

statewide_baseline.quote: An “electric bicycle” is a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts of power.

jurisdictions.covers: All public rights-of-way, parks, paths, trails and any other area open to bicycle travel in the City (SDMC 84.19). Includes Carmel Valley, Pacific Highlands Ranch and the Canyon Crest Academy area. The neighborhood list is carried over from the earlier record, not from the ordinance.
jurisdictions.verified_note: Read in enacted text on Oct 19, 2026. Ordinance O-22123 N.S. adds SDMC 84.19 (under-12 ban), 84.20 (enforcement) and 84.21 (helmets and passengers). Introduced Jun 23, 2026, passed by Council Jul 7, 2026 (Item 51), final passage Jul 14, 2026, effective Aug 13, 2026. The signed ordinance and the codified 8-2026 SDMC Ch. 8 Art. 4 match word for word. SDMC 84.04, 84.09, 84.18, 63.0102 and 63.0109 were also read.

local_age_limits.quote: Persons under 12 years of age are prohibited from operating Class 1 and Class 2 electric bicycles. This prohibition applies to all public rights-of-way, parks, paths, trails, and any other area open to bicycle travel.
local_age_limits.notes: Adopted under VC 21214.7(b), final passage Jul 14, 2026. Infraction with a $25 fine (SDMC 84.20(b)(1)), after warnings only for the first 60 days (SDMC 84.20(a), VC 21214.7(c)(1)(A)). A parent or legal guardian with custody or control of an unemancipated minor is jointly and severally liable (SDMC 84.20(b)(3)). The enacted text gives no calendar date for the first citation. The City release gives Oct 12, 2026. A count under Code Civ. Proc. 12 (excluding Aug 13) makes Oct 12 the 60th warning day, so Oct 13 would be the first citation day under that reading. The app keeps Oct 12, the City's date and the earlier one. The ordinance is repealed Jan 1, 2029 (O-22123 N.S. Sec. 2, and the editor's note to SDMC 84.19) unless the VC 21214.7 sunset is extended or made permanent, in which case it stays in effect as long as the state law does, so the end date must track the statute. That sunset also covers the SDMC 84.21 helmet and passenger rules.

tag_and_course_requirements.quote: no fine shall be imposed if the parent or legal guardian of the person who violated section 84.19 provides proof to the City, within 120 days of the citation, that the person has completed an electric bicycle safety and training program under California Streets and Highways Code section 894.
tag_and_course_requirements.notes: Sts. & Hy. Code 894(c) requires the CHP program to be posted on the CHP website.

helmet_rules.citation: SDMC 84.21(a) and (c) (O-22123 N.S.), Cal. Veh. Code 21212, 21213
helmet_rules.quote: All operators and passengers of electric bicycles shall comply with the helmet requirements in the California Vehicle Code, including sections 21212 and 21213. Helmets shall be properly fitted and fastened at all times while operating the electric bicycle. ... Section 84.21 applies to all electric bicycle operators.
helmet_rules.notes: 84.21(a) incorporates state helmet law, under 18 on any e-bike and all ages on Class 3 (VC 21212(a), 21213(b)), and says helmets shall be properly fitted and fastened at all times while operating. 84.21(c) says the section applies to all electric bicycle operators. Recital F says the Council intends to reinforce existing state requirements, so one reading only requires required helmets to be fitted and fastened, but (c) supports a helmet rule for every operator. That question is open, so a City answer always lists a helmet for every rider, at any age (lib/rules/local.ts, sd_helmet_all_riders). Text read in the 8-2026 SDMC Ch. 8 Art. 4 PDF on Oct 19, 2026, matching O-22123 N.S. page 4. The section ends Jan 1, 2029 with the rest of O-22123 unless the VC 21214.7 sunset is extended. The app keeps the helmet line after that, since wearing one is never wrong.

emoto_enforcement.quote: A person is operating a vehicle with fewer than four wheels that does not meet the definition of an electric bicycle set forth in Section 312.5 and is both of the following: (A) Powered by an electric motor capable of exclusively propelling the vehicle in excess of 20 miles per hour on a highway.
emoto_enforcement.notes: No City e-moto ordinance was found. SDMC 82.32 only says police impounds follow the Vehicle Code. Verdict stays not an e-bike.

other_local_rules.quote: Electric bicycle operators are prohibited from carrying a passenger unless the electric bicycle is specifically designed and manufactured to carry more than one person and is equipped with a separate seat or saddle for each passenger
other_local_rules.notes: Stricter than VC 21204(b), which only requires a separate seat attached to the bicycle. An aftermarket seat that is legal under state law is not enough in the City. Repealed Jan 1, 2029 with the rest of O-22123 unless the VC 21214.7 sunset is extended.

other_local_rules.quote: It is unlawful for any person to operate any motorized transportation device in the following locations: (1) on the public walkway on Ocean Front Walk in Mission Beach
other_local_rules.notes: A motorized transportation device includes an electric bicycle, rented or owned (SDMC 83.0302 uses the VC 312.5 meaning). Covers Ocean Front Walk (South Mission Beach Jetty to Law St), Bayside Walk (San Diego Place to Corona Oriente Rd), the east Mission Bay walkway (De Anza Rd to South Shores) and the La Jolla Shores boardwalk (Avenida De La Playa to Kellogg Park). Exceptions for physically disabled persons and City law enforcement.

other_local_rules.quote: No person shall operate a bicycle upon any sidewalk fronting any commercial business establishment unless official signs are posted authorizing such use.
other_local_rules.notes: VC 231 says an electric bicycle is a bicycle, and SDMC 81.0101 adopts Vehicle Code definitions, so 84.09(a) reaches e-bikes. SDMC 84.04 separately bars riding any vehicle on any sidewalk, and VC 670 excludes only devices moved exclusively by human power, so an e-bike may count as a vehicle under 84.04. Whether e-bikes may ride on other sidewalks is unclear, so the app never implies they may. SDMC 84.09 was last amended in 1992.

other_local_rules.quote: Bicycles. It is unlawful to ride a bicycle except: (1) where posted to authorize bicycle riding; or (2) on any designated bikeway; or (3) on any road designated and established for automotive traffic; or (4) on paved and unpaved roads within a park used as fire or service roads by authorized motor vehicles unless otherwise posted. Motorcycles or any other motorized vehicles are prohibited except on roads designated and established for automotive traffic.
other_local_rules.notes: Parks by definition include open space, beaches and perimeter sidewalks (SDMC 63.0102(b)). Treat e-bikes on park paths that are not posted or designated bikeways as not allowed. Whether an e-bike is a motorized vehicle under this section is unclear. SDMC 63.0109 sets an 8 mph limit for all wheeled transport on Ocean Front Walk and listed Mission Bay paths. Read in the 9-2024 edition.

conflicts_with_statute.source_says: The Aug 7 release says the rules make 'a pedal bike the only bike approved for ages 12 and under'.
conflicts_with_statute.statute_says: VC 21214.7(b) allows a ban only for riders 'under 12 years of age'. The same release also says 'If your child is under 12'.
conflicts_with_statute.engine_rule: Treat 12-year-olds as allowed on Class 1 and 2 unless the ordinance text says otherwise. An ordinance cannot go past the statute.
conflicts_with_statute.resolved: Resolved by the enacted text. SDMC 84.19 (O-22123 N.S.) says 'Persons under 12 years of age', matching VC 21214.7(b). A 12-year-old is not banned.

open_questions: Whether SDMC 84.04 (no vehicles on any sidewalk) reaches e-bikes on sidewalks that do not front a business. Until settled, the app never says those sidewalks are allowed.
Whether an e-bike counts as a 'motorized vehicle' under SDMC 63.0102(c)(19) inside City parks.

resolved_questions.answer: O-22123 N.S. adds SDMC 84.19, 84.20 and 84.21. Final passage Jul 14, 2026, effective Aug 13, 2026.

resolved_questions.answer: SDMC 84.19 says 'under 12', as the statute allows. A 12-year-old may ride Class 1 or 2 under City law.

resolved_questions.question: Reports say the ban covers streets, bike paths, parks, trails and boardwalks. Not confirmed in an official City source.
resolved_questions.answer: SDMC 84.19 applies to all public rights-of-way, parks, paths, trails and any other area open to bicycle travel.

local_age_limits.quote: No person under 12 years of age may operate or ride a Class 1 electric bicycle or Class 2 electric bicycle within the city.
local_age_limits.citations_from_citation: Carlsbad staff report, Feb 10, 2026, packet p. 341
local_age_limits.notes: Adopted under VC 21214.7(b) by Ord. CS-509 (adopted Feb 24, 2026, effective Mar 26, 2026). Warnings for the first 60 days under VC 21214.7(c)(1)(A). The Feb 10, 2026 staff report says the warning period ends May 25, 2026, so citations can start May 26. No end date. Unlike SDMC 84.19, the enacted CMC 10.56.030(A) has no sunset clause, and CS-509 says only that it takes effect thirty days after adoption (Feb 24, 2026 packet p. 258). Whether the ban still applies after VC 21214.7 is repealed on Jan 1, 2029 is unsettled, so from that date the app says it can't confirm, never yes. Covers Class 1 and 2 only. Class 3 is already 16+ under state law. By its text the section also bars under-12 passengers (see under_12_passenger_ban).

tag_and_course_requirements.quote: shall be released after a minimum of 48 hours, if both of the following conditions are met: 1. The minor operator has completed, in person at the police station, a Police Department approved electric bicycle safety and training program.
tag_and_course_requirements.notes: Applies to an e-bike operated by a minor, after a violation that creates an immediate or substantial risk. Held at least 48 hours, the course is taken in person at the police station and a parent or guardian must be present at release. No payment can substitute.

helmet_rules.citation: Carlsbad Mun. Code 10.56.020(C)(1)(g)-(h) (Ord. CS-509), Cal. Veh. Code 21212(a), 21213
helmet_rules.quote: g. Ride without a properly fitted and fastened helmet, if under 18 years of age. h. Ride a Class 3 electric bicycle without a properly fitted and fastened helmet, regardless of age.
helmet_rules.notes: Both items are new in CS-509, so the local effective date is Mar 26, 2026. VC 21212(a) already applied.

emoto_enforcement.citation: Cal. Veh. Code 22651.08(a)(1) (AB 875), Carlsbad Mun. Code 10.56.045
emoto_enforcement.quote: (A) Powered by an electric motor capable of exclusively propelling the vehicle in excess of 20 miles per hour on a highway. (B) Being operated by an operator who is not licensed to operate the vehicle.
emoto_enforcement.notes: No local e-motorcycle impound section was found in the Carlsbad code. CMC 10.56.045 adds only cost recovery. The city page names Sur-Ron, Talaria, 79-Bike, Rawrr Mantis and Stark as e-motorcycles needing a motorcycle endorsement, registration and insurance.

other_local_rules.quote: That Poinsettia Community Park and Pine Avenue Community Park are added to the list of locations where electric bicycles are prohibited pursuant to Carlsbad Municipal Code Section 10.56.020(A).
other_local_rules.notes: A council resolution, not part of CS-509. Under CMC 10.56.020(A) as it stood before CS-509, a resolution adds places to the list directly, and the ban applies where signs are posted. Walking a bike through stays allowed unless posted (staff report p. 341). Only the unsigned packet draft was read. It says 'RESOLUTION NO. ___' and leaves the adoption date blank. The Feb 10, 2026 minutes (doc 25575, page 14) show it adopted that day, 5/0. Neither text gives an effective date, and the date the signs went up is unknown, so no effective date is shown.

other_local_rules.quote: Transport any other person upon the bar, handle bars, floorboard or other area of a regulated mobility device not designed for passenger riding or transport any other person on a regulated mobility device designed for a single rider.
other_local_rules.notes: In force before Ord. CS-509. In the CS-509 redline (Feb 10, 2026 packet p. 350) the passenger language is unchanged black text, and only the reworded ending is red. The city's e-bike page reprints the old 10.56.020(C)(1), which already barred carrying a person on a device not designed for passengers.

other_local_rules.quote: No person shall operate or ride a regulated mobility device upon any sidewalk, in any public drainage facility, culvert, ditch, channel, or any other public athletic/sports court, or gymnasium in the city.
other_local_rules.notes: In force before Ord. CS-509, which left this wording unchanged (black text in the Feb 10, 2026 packet p. 350 redline). Covers every e-bike class and pedal bikes. CMC 10.32.030 (Ord. 3005) separately bars vehicles, including bicycles, from any sidewalk area. CMC 11.32.070 makes the seawall sidewalk between Tamarack Ave and Pine St pedestrians only.

other_local_rules.quote: "Rider" means a traveler riding in or on a regulated mobility device who is not operating it.
other_local_rules.notes: By its text, CMC 10.56.030(A) bars anyone under 12 from riding a Class 1 or 2 e-bike as a passenger, not only from operating one. The Feb 10, 2026 staff report (p. 340) also says 'operating or riding'. VC 21214.7(b) authorizes a ban only on operating, so the local text goes further than the enabling statute, and the city's own page describes an operator ban only.

other_local_rules.quote: This chapter is not intended to apply to or otherwise restrict regulated mobility devices used in a safe manner by physically disabled persons as defined under the Americans with Disabilities Act
other_local_rules.notes: Covers the whole chapter, including the under-12 ban in 10.56.030. Unchanged by CS-509. The app can't assess disability or safe use, so an under-12 verdict stays no with this note.

other_local_rules.quote: must dismount the regulated mobility device where the trail width is less than five feet and a pedestrian or equine is within a distance of 50 feet from the regulated mobility device.
other_local_rules.notes: A conduct rule, not a legality gate.

other_local_rules.quote: To use or operate any vehicles at any time, except as permitted by the City Manager, or designee, in a park, designated streets or parking areas or as part of a supervised recreational activity
other_local_rules.notes: Whether an e-bike is a 'vehicle' under CMC 10.04.150, which excludes 'a device moved by human power', is unclear, and City Manager permissions were not found. The city adopted a separate resolution to ban e-bikes in only two parks and its flier says 'Some*' parks, so the app does not treat this as a park ban for Class 1 and 2. CMC 11.32.010 counts public trails as parks. The city flier says Class 3 is not allowed on trails (see class3_trails_city_flier), so Class 3 on trails stays unclear.

The page 1 table has an 'Allowed on trails' row, and its Class 3 column says No (read Oct 19, 2026). No verbatim quote was recorded. A city flier, not enacted text, so it backs a note and never a verdict.

conflicts_with_statute.source_says: The page defines an e-bike as having 'an electric motor of less than 750 watts' and reprints that wording as VC 312.5(a).
conflicts_with_statute.statute_says: Since Jan 1, 2025, VC 312.5(a) says the motor 'does not exceed 750 watts of power'.
conflicts_with_statute.citation: Cal. Veh. Code 312.5(a); Carlsbad Mun. Code 10.56.010, 10.56.015
conflicts_with_statute.engine_rule: Use the statute. A 750 W label passes in California.

conflicts_with_statute.source_says: Class 3 is 'Allowed in bike lanes or separated bikeways adjacent to the roadway', and Class 4 bikeways are for 'Only Types 1 and 2'.
conflicts_with_statute.statute_says: Since AB 1909 (Jan 1, 2023) VC 21207.5 has no state Class 3 ban on bike paths or bikeways. No Carlsbad code singles out Class 3. But CMC 11.32.010 counts public trails as parks, and CMC 11.32.030(22) bars operating any vehicle in a park except as the City Manager permits.
conflicts_with_statute.engine_rule: Show Class 3 on bike lanes and bikeways as not banned by Carlsbad code. Keep Class 3 on trails unclear.

open_questions: Whether e-bikes are 'vehicles' under CMC 10.04.150, so that CMC 11.32.030(22) bars them in parks and on public trails, and what the City Manager has permitted. The city says Class 3 is not allowed on trails.

local_age_limits.citation: Encinitas Council Agenda Report, Aug 19, 2026, Item 12C
local_age_limits.quote: Amending the EMC to require e-bike riders to be 12 years old would make Encinitas consistent with those cities.
local_age_limits.notes: No age provision in EMC Ch. 14.56 (https://ecode360.com/44479706) or anywhere else in the code read on Oct 19, 2026. The quote is a staff proposal on page 3 of the Aug 19, 2026 agenda report (footer 'Item #12C Page 3 of 14'), not code text. Council discussed a minimum age of 12 on Aug 19, 2026 (Item 12C). Per the minutes, staff will return with proposed code amendments at a future meeting. No ordinance was introduced or adopted through the Oct 21, 2026 agenda. A new ordinance needs two readings and normally takes effect 30 days after adoption.

helmet_rules.quote: A person under 18 years of age shall not operate a bicycle, a nonmotorized scooter, or a skateboard
helmet_rules.notes: Matches the city page ('17 and under'). The only EMC helmet rule is 9.50.030, which covers skate parks. Class 3 needs a helmet at all ages (VC 21213(b)).

emoto_enforcement.quote: It is unlawful for any person to operate any motorcycle or power cycle on any trails used by hikers, horse riders or bicyclist.
emoto_enforcement.notes: EMC 8.04.010 and 8.04.130 bar self-propelled vehicles, mopeds and motorcycles from city beaches, parks and recreational trails except on authorized roadways. An e-moto is a motorcycle and a self-propelled vehicle under these sections. State tow authority is VC 22651.08 (see statewide_baseline). Do not use 14.32.093 against legal e-bikes, because 'power cycle' is undefined.

other_local_rules.quote: No person shall ride a bicycle on a sidewalk within a business district.
other_local_rules.notes: The sections come from Ord. 2019-26 and Ord. 2023-10. The business district is not limited to South Coast Highway 101 from D Street to J Street. EMC 14.06.030 says it 'shall include' that segment, and EMC 14.06.010 applies Vehicle Code definitions, so any area that meets VC 235 also counts. EMC 14.06.020 and VC 231 make e-bikes bicycles. EMC 14.56.020(C) requires yielding to pedestrians on any sidewalk, and 14.56.020(A) allows posted signs. The app never says sidewalk riding is allowed elsewhere.

other_local_rules.quote: It is unlawful for any person to drive, park or allow to stand any self propelled vehicle on a public beach, public park, or recreational trail unless the operator has previously obtained express approval
other_local_rules.notes: Title 8 does not define vehicle, and EMC 14.06.010 imports Vehicle Code definitions only into Title 14. VC 670 excludes only devices moved exclusively by human power, so these sections may reach e-bikes. The city e-bike page says Type 1 and 2 are allowed on trails marked for bicycles, and the Aug 2026 staff report lists a park ban only as a new option. Shown as unclear, never as allowed and never as clearly banned.

other_local_rules.quote: It shall be unlawful for the operator of any bicycle to carry any other person upon the handle- bars of any such bicycle for any person to so ride, or in any other manner not designed for passenger riding, upon any such bicycle upon any highway or public place.(Ord. 2023-05)
other_local_rules.notes: Class-neutral. Ord. 2023-05 was adopted Jun 28, 2023 and took effect 30 days later.

other_local_rules.quote: the police chief or designee may allow a first-time violator of this chapter to complete a police department-approved bicycle safety course.(Ord. 2023-05)
other_local_rules.notes: Discretionary, not a condition of riding.

tag_and_course_requirements.quote: Students who do not have a Bike Tag visibly affixed to their bicycle will not be permitted to bring it onto any SDUHSD campus.
tag_and_course_requirements.notes: Parents complete the online tag form after training. Tags can be revoked. No board policy number. Presented to the Board as information item 4.B, June 17, 2026, no vote.

tag_and_course_requirements.quote: All middle and high school students must complete an approved safety training program.
tag_and_course_requirements.notes: High school students use the CHP online e-bike course or a quarterly in-person class. The Canyon Crest Academy in-person date is Dec 9, 2026. This rests on the district program, not on a board policy. AR 5142 says only that training 'may' be provided, and the Board took no vote.

helmet_rules.quote: Any student who rides any such bicycle, scooter, skateboard, or roller skates at school shall wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet.
helmet_rules.notes: No age cutoff, so it reaches 18-year-old seniors whom state law does not cover. 'Such bicycle' refers back to electric, motorized or nonmotorized bicycles. The district Bike Safety page repeats it. The Simbli link is version-specific, so re-check it after any AR 5142 revision.

emoto_enforcement.quote: Only Class 1 & Class 2 E-Bikes will be permitted on our campuses.
emoto_enforcement.notes: Same sentence as class_1_and_2_only_on_campus, so the same date, the first school day (Aug 11, 2026). The Aug 28, 2026 grace period covers only training and tags. A district administrative rule. No enacted SDUHSD text names e-motos. AR 5142 lists 'Motorcycling' among activities a principal may not permit on campus unless supervised, which is only loose support. The 'not road legal' wording appears only in Aug 6 and Sep 10, 2026 staff summaries. If a revised AR 5142 with personal transportation device text is posted, cite it as primary.

other_local_rules.quote: Passengers are permitted to ride only on bikes with a factory-installed passenger seat and must wear a properly secured bike helmet.
other_local_rules.notes: Dated to the first school day (Aug 11, 2026), like class_1_and_2_only_on_campus. The page's only dated sentence gives a grace period until Aug 28, 2026, and it covers only training and tags. Bikes must also be walked on school grounds, and campus charging is not allowed. No adopted BP or AR covers walking, passengers or charging. The walking rule appears only in the staff summary of the CSBA regulation update, and a revised AR 5142 may add it later.

open_questions: Whether the tag and class rules apply to bikes parked just off campus.

Watch for a revised AR 5142 with the CSBA personal transportation device text (described at the Aug 6 and Sep 10, 2026 meetings, item 11.D). Its road-legal wording may conflict with the page's Class 1 and 2 only rule.

resolved_questions.question: Board policy or administrative regulation number behind the page.
resolved_questions.answer: None for the class, tag or course rules. The only related texts are AR 5142 (site rules and helmets) and BP and AR 5142.2. The Board heard the program as information item 4.B on June 17, 2026 with no motion.
